skill.name: sync-before-work
skill.description: Synchronizes the current Git branch with the latest remote default branch before code changes. It checks repository state and blocks unsafe operations.
skill.summary: Update a Git branch from its remote default branch before editing.
skill.author: vaibhavarora14

security_audit.summary: Most detections confuse JavaScript template literals, Markdown formatting, or normal environment inheritance with shell or sensitive-file access. The Git subprocess is intentional, but merge and rebase can execute configured hooks under the current user account.

remediation.issue: Git merge and rebase may execute hooks configured in the working repository.
remediation.suggestion: Disable hooks for automated synchronization, or require explicit user approval before any apply operation that can merge or rebase.

remediation.issue: The Git subprocess inherits the complete process environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal allowlist of required environment variables and exclude unrelated credentials from the child process.

content.value_statement: Code changes can begin from an outdated branch and create avoidable conflicts. This skill checks remote state and safely incorporates the default branch.
actual_capabilities: Detects the current branch, configured remotes, and remote default branch.
Blocks apply mode when the worktree is dirty or Git operations are active.
Fetches the selected remote branch in preview and apply modes.
Merges divergent feature branches by default and rebases unpublished branches only when requested.
Aborts failed merges or rebases and verifies that the original commit was restored.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20 or newer and an installed Git command.
Check mode uses cached remote references and may report stale state.
Apply mode can change local commit history or create a merge commit.
Repository hooks and configured Git helpers may run during Git operations.

prompt_templates.title: Check synchronization status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this branch includes the latest remote default branch. Do not fetch or change files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use local references for a read-only check.

prompt_templates.title: Preview the update
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the remote default branch and preview the required synchronization. Do not change the current branch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect current remote state before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Synchronize safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Synchronize this clean branch with the latest remote default branch using the default merge strategy. Stop on any safety refusal.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a feature branch before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Rebase an unpublished branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that this branch is unpublished, then synchronize it by rebasing onto the latest remote default branch. Stop if publication is detected.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an explicit rebase for private local work.

output_examples.input: Check this repository without network access.
output_examples.output: The current branch already contains the locally cached default branch. No files or commits changed.

output_examples.input: Preview synchronization with the latest remote state.
output_examples.output: The remote default branch was fetched. The current branch can fast-forward, but preview mode made no branch change.

output_examples.input: Synchronize this feature branch before editing.
output_examples.output: Synchronization stopped because the worktree contains local changes. Commit or remove them before applying the update.

best_practices: Use preview mode when branch ownership or the expected operation is uncertain.
Keep merge as the default strategy for shared or published branches.
Review any reported merge, rebase, or recovery result before editing.
anti_patterns: Do not apply synchronization to a dirty worktree.
Do not request rebase for published or shared branches.
Do not ignore a conflict, recovery failure, or safety refusal.

faq.question: Does the skill push changes?
faq.answer: No. It only reads remote state and changes the current local branch when apply mode permits.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Check mode uses local references, but those references may be stale.

faq.question: What happens with uncommitted files?
faq.answer: Apply mode stops when staged, unstaged, or untracked files exist.

faq.question: When does it use rebase?
faq.answer: Rebase requires explicit selection and is refused when the branch appears published.

faq.question: How are conflicts handled?
faq.answer: The script aborts the merge or rebase and verifies restoration of the original commit.

faq.question: Can Git hooks run?
faq.answer: Yes. Configured hooks may run during merge or rebase operations with the current user's permissions.
